nodes.summary: Let each activity $a$ have a start time $s(a)$ and a finish time $f(a)$ in a linearly ordered type, thought of as the closed-open interval $[s(a), f(a))$. Two activities $a$ and $b$ are compatible when $f(a) \le s(b)$ or $f(b) \le s(a)$; in particular, activities whose intervals only touch at an endpoint are compatible.
nodes.title: Compatible activities

nodes.summary: Let $s$ and $f$ assign start and finish times in a linear order to activities, and let $L$ be a list of activities with $s(a) < f(a)$ for every $a$ in $L$. Let $S$ be the list returned by the earliest-finish schedule of $L$. nodes.title: Correctness and optimality of earliest-finish interval scheduling

nodes.summary: For any start and finish times and any list of $n$ activities, the earliest-finish schedule charges at most $n \lceil \log_2 n \rceil + (n - 1)$ comparisons when $n \ge 1$, and none when $n = 0$.
nodes.title: Comparison bound for earliest-finish interval scheduling

nodes.summary: Given start and finish times $s$ and $f$ in a linear order and a list $L$ of activities, sort $L$ by finish time with merge sort, then scan the sorted list: the first activity is selected, and each later activity $a$ is selected exactly when $s(a)$ is at least the finish time of the last selected activity. nodes.title: Earliest-finish greedy interval scheduling

nodes.summary: For any start and finish times and any activities $a$ and $b$, if $a$ is compatible with $b$, then $b$ is compatible with $a$.
nodes.title: Symmetry of interval compatibility

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
